content.title: About
content.content: Cereal Corn Squares are crunchy dry breakfast pieces made from whole corn, coated with a flavorful fruit or berry glaze. They are suitable for a quick breakfast, snack, or addition to milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn squares first appeared in the United States in the 1970s as an alternative to traditional flakes.
The glaze may contain natural flavorings such as berries, citrus, or vanilla.
The product is often used in children's breakfasts and as an ingredient in dessert bars.
Corn, the base ingredient, is rich in antioxidant carotenoids.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn provides slowly digestible carbs that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Contains B vitamins
items.content: The product includes B‑group vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Corn squares typically contain less than 2 % fat, making them a light snack.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber helps maintain normal bowel function.

items.title: Fortified with iron
items.content: Many versions are enriched with iron, beneficial for blood formation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The glaze may contain added sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Corn squares can raise blood glucose levels quickly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the squares dry, add them to milk, yogurt, or smoothies. They can also be used in baking, sprinkled over ice cream, or incorporated into dessert cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, keep in the refrigerator to preserve crispness.
